diagnostic_evidence.quote: As a byproduct, we prove the existence and uniqueness of the periodic fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK} in $H^{r}_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)$, $r\geq 1+\alpha$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction claim the rate N^{-r} for initial data in H^r. The error theorem instead assumes u in C^1([0,T];H^r), and its proof uses |∂_t u|_r. Since ∂_t u = ∂_{x1}(-Δ)^{α/2}u - u∂_{x1}u, this requires u(t) in H^{r+1+α}, i.e. data about α+1 orders smoother, plus a persistence-of-regularity result that is never proved. Existence is also treated only in H^{1+α}, so the claimed existence and uniqueness in H^r for every r≥1+α is not proved either.

failure_location.quote: The method achieves spectral convergence of order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-r})$ for initial data in $H^r_{\mathrm{per}}$ with $r \geq \alpha+1$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claims as in the theorem: rate N^{-r} for solutions with u in C^1([0,T];H^r), i.e. data in H^{r+1+α} given persistence of regularity. Remove the H^r existence claim or prove persistence of H^r regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The headline relation between data regularity and convergence rate, and the H^r well-posedness byproduct, are overstated.
issues.title: Advertised N^{-r} rate for H^r data and H^r well-posedness are not established
issues.why_classification: The formal theorem survives under its own hypotheses, but the advertised rate for given data regularity is weakened by about α+1 orders.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.

issues.failure_explanation: Both sides of the claimed inequality are bilinear in (f,g). Applying it to (f,-g) gives the reverse inequality, which would force equality for all f,g; that is false. Concretely, for α=2, f=sin x1, g=-sin x1: the left side is 2cos2x1 and the right side is 2cos2x1-2. A one-sided pointwise bound also cannot imply the 'consequent' norm bound, and the proof is only a citation. In est_nonl the lemma is used to bound |((-Δ)^{(1+α)/2}(u_N∂u_N),(-Δ)^{(1+α)/2}u_N)| by absolute values of two other inner products. That does not follow even from the pointwise claim, because the test function changes sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the pointwise claim and use a Kato–Ponce commutator estimate ||[(-Δ)^{s/2},f]g|| ≲ ||∇f||_∞||g||_{s-1}+||f||_s||g||_∞. Then redo est_nonl: integrate by parts in the u_N∂(-Δ)^{s/2}u_N term and bound the commutator.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform H^{1+α} bound (bd3) and everything built on it lack a valid proof.
issues.title: False pointwise fractional product inequality, misused in the H^{1+α} energy estimate
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument using a standard estimate restores the energy bound without changing results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Sobolev embedding $H^{1+\alpha}(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$:

issues.failure_explanation: The last step of est_nonl needs ||∂_{x1}u_N||_∞ ≤ C||u_N||_{1+α} uniformly in N, i.e. H^α(T^2) ↪ L^∞. This holds only for α>1 and fails at α=1, since H^1(T^2) is not in L^∞. The only embedding in the paper, lem:inverse_inequalities(ii), carries a factor 3N and so destroys N-uniformity. The same gap appears in three other places. The uniqueness proof needs ∂_{x1}ū in L^∞ but invokes only H^{1+α} ↪ L^∞. The spectral error proof uses ||∂f||_∞ ≤ C|f|_2, which is false in 2D. And bounding ||∂_{x1}u_N||_∞ there via bd3 has the same α=1 failure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use H^s(T^2) ↪ W^{1,∞} for s>2, which covers α>1. At α=1, require data in H^{2+ε} or exclude α=1. Replace |·|_2 by an H^{2+ε} norm in the spectral proof.
issues.overall_effect: At α=1 the uniform bound, uniqueness and error estimate are unproved. For α>1 they rely on an embedding the paper never correctly invokes.
issues.title: W^{1,∞} control from H^{1+α} fails at α=1; only an N-dependent embedding is available
issues.why_classification: The results survive for α>1, and survive at α=1 under slightly stronger data, which is a limited weakening.

issues.failure_explanation: Arzelà–Ascoli in C([0,T];L^2) requires pointwise relative compactness in L^2. A bounded set in the infinite-dimensional space L^2 is not relatively compact, so equicontinuity plus bd1 does not yield a convergent subsequence.

failure_location.quote: Combined with the uniform boundedness in $L^2_{\text{per}}(\Omega)$ from \eqref{bd1}, the Arzelà-Ascoli theorem guaranties the existence of a subsequence

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use bd3 together with the compact (Rellich) embedding H^{1+α} ↪ L^2 to get pointwise relative compactness.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the extraction of a convergent subsequence, and hence existence, is unjustified.
issues.title: Arzelà–Ascoli applied with only an L^2 bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix using a bound already proved preserves the claims.

issues.failure_explanation: bd3 holds only for t ≤ T̄ = 1/(C||u_0||_{1+α}), and only gives a bound of 2||u_0||_{1+α}. Restarting at T̄ with norm up to 2||u_0|| gives a step of T̄/2, then T̄/4, and so on, so the total time is at most 2T̄ and arbitrary T is never reached. The conserved mass, momentum and Hamiltonian control only L^2 and H^{α/2}, not H^{1+α}.

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish an N-uniform a priori bound on ||u_N(t)||_{1+α} on arbitrary [0,T], or restrict the results to the local interval [0,T̄].
issues.overall_effect: Global existence and uniqueness on every [0,T] is unproved. The spectral error proof's use of bd3 on [0,T] is justified only up to T̄.
issues.title: Continuation to arbitrary time relies on a non-existent time-uniform H^{1+α} bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $w \in H^r_{\text{per}}(\Omega)$ with $r \geq 1+\alpha$, we define the modified projection
we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology

While the adaptation from the one-dimensional Kawahara setting to our multidimensional fractional ZK equation requires careful handling of the fractional Laplacian and the additional spatial dimension

issues.failure_explanation: The projection Π̃_N is defined, and shown solvable, only for r ≥ 1+α, yet the estimates are claimed for all r ≥ 0. No proof is given: the cited 1D Kawahara result concerns a different operator, and the paper admits the adaptation is nontrivial. A direct energy argument yields only ||Π̃_N w - Π_N w|| ≲ ||u||_∞||∂(w-Π_N w)|| = O(N^{1-r}), one order short. The optimal rate needs the omitted duality argument, and time_error needs differentiation of a projection with a time-dependent coefficient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to r ≥ 1+α. Supply proofs of the coercivity/duality estimates for the operator K+u∂_{x1}-(-Δ)^{α/2}∂_{x1} in 2D, including the time-derivative version.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal N^{-r} error bound rests on unproved estimates.
issues.title: Modified-projection error estimates unproved and stated beyond the projection's domain
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial new proof is required; the stated rates are plausible to recover.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we assume that $r$ is proportional to $N$.
There exists a constant $C > 0$ independent of $N$ such that:

issues.failure_explanation: The bound |w|_r ≤ r!||w|| is false: for w = e^{iMx1}, |w|_r/||w|| grows like M^r and is unbounded for fixed r. For analytic w the correct bound depends on the analyticity strip, not on ||w||. Moreover, C in proj_erro may depend on r, so letting r grow proportionally to N requires explicit control of C(r), which is not available. The √r Stirling factor is also dropped.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the exponential bound directly: use the exponential Fourier decay of analytic w for Π_N, plus N-uniform stability of Π̃_N relative to Π_N, with constants depending on w's analyticity strip.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential projection estimate proj_erro2, and the exponential convergence claim, are unproved.
issues.title: Invalid 'Stirling' derivation of exponential projection error
issues.why_classification: A new but contained argument is required; a comparable exponential statement plausibly survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If, in addition, the initial data \(u_0\) is real-analytic

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes only that u_0 is analytic. The proof, however, applies proj_erro2 to the solution u(t), which needs u(t) analytic for all t; persistence of analyticity for fZK is never shown. It also bounds the term with ∂_t(Π̃_N u - u) by Ce^{-σN}, although only algebraic rates (lem:time_error) are available for the time derivative.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = e^{-L t} \mathcal{N}\left( e^{L t} V(t) \right) =: \mathcal{F}(t, V(t)).
where all derivatives be evaluated at $(t_n, V^n)$.
$r \geq \alpha + 5$, and assume the nonlinear term $\mathcal{N}$ is sufficiently smooth

issues.failure_explanation: F depends on t through e^{±Lt} with ||L|| ~ N^{1+α}, so ∂_t^k F contains L^k. The Taylor remainders therefore grow like N^{k(1+α)} unless offset by smoothness of the trajectory. That trajectory starts at the numerical V^n, whose smoothness is not controlled. Each time derivative costs about 1+α spatial derivatives, so r ≥ α+5 cannot give an N-uniform O(Δt^5) bound. The uniformity is simply asserted.

failure_location.quote: Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out a stiff-order error analysis using defects of the exact solution, with explicitly stronger regularity (about 4–5 multiples of 1+α derivatives).
issues.overall_effect: The fourth-order temporal accuracy uniform in N is unproved.
issues.title: IF-RK4 local error constant claimed N-uniform without justification
issues.why_classification: A new contained analysis with stronger hypotheses yields a comparable fourth-order result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The global error accumulates as $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^4)$ over $\mathcal{O}(1/\Delta t)$ time steps.
consider the linearized version of the fZK equation where the nonlinear term is replaced by \(\lambda \partial_{x_1} u\)

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims a fully discrete estimate with C_2 independent of N and Δt, and 'optimal convergence rates in both space and time'. It establishes only a local truncation bound and linear stability for a frozen-coefficient model. The Lipschitz constant of F in V grows like N||u_N||_∞ because of the factor m_1. Accumulating local errors therefore needs a nonlinear stability proof, a step-size restriction Δt ≲ 1/N, and an a priori bound on the numerical solution; none is provided.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove convergence of the nonlinear IF-RK4 scheme under an explicit condition Δt ≤ c/N, using an induction-based bound on the numerical solution combined with the local error estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised fully discrete error analysis and the space–time convergence claim are unsupported.
issues.title: Fully discrete error bound asserted without nonlinear stability analysis
issues.why_classification: It needs a new but standard convergence argument, probably with an explicit step-size restriction.
